papers.title: Sleep and memory in adolescents
pages:
Sleep and Memory in Adolescents
A. Author, B. Author
Contact: a.author@uni.edu
Abstract. Sleeping well improves memory consolidation in adolescents. We tested 120 students across two schools. Results showed that sleep duration predicted recall.
Method. Participants slept in the lab. Memory was tested with word lists & picture tasks. The "quotes" of participants were recorded; it's noted that students' sleep varied < 7 hours > 5 hours.
Discussion. Short sleep impaired recall. Limitations include the small sample and self-reported sleep diaries. Future studies should test anxiety.

papers.title: Screen time & anxiety
pages:
Short
Screen time and anxiety among adolescents: a survey of 2,000 pupils
Correspondence to x_y-z@mail.example.org.
Anxiety scores rose with screen use. Adolescents who used phones at night reported worse sleep. Anxiety, anxiety and more anxiety. Re-testing after a re-test showed the same.

papers.title: A long page
pages: Introduction.	This   page is long on purpose. It talks about many things before the topic arrives, such as weather, gardens, trains, rivers and other matters that are not the point at all. It goes on and on for a while so that the snippet has to cut the text on both sides. Then at last the key word working memory appears in the middle of the page, followed by more filler text about clouds, mountains, valleys, oceans and deserts that keeps the page going well past the end of the snippet window so that it is cut there too. Finally a sentence about sleep and memory and adolescents ends the page!
